newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Jelmoli may gain capital for investment.
newsitem.headline: Jelmoli may gain capital for investment.

text.p: A recent shuffle in ownership among big Swiss retailers may give Jelmoli Holding AG more capital to invest, said Jelmoli's majority owner Walter Fust.
Fust, a Swiss investor, gained a majority stake in Jelmoli last November.

In July, Swiss retailing cooperative MIGROS- Genossenschafts-Bund announced it planned to acquire over 50 percent of the voting capital of Jelmoli's rival retailer Magazine zum Globus, and offered to buy the rest of its shares.
Globus rents retail stores from Jelmoli, which underwent a restructuring over recent years.
In an interview published on Saturday in the Berner Zeitung daily, Fust said properties rented by Globus from Jelmoli were valued at 350-400 million Swiss francs.
With the capital from an eventual sale of the property to Globus, "we could certainly get more than the rent," Fust said.
But in the case of any such sale, the price would have to meet Fust's "high expectations," he added.
He also did not rule out a cooperation or other "synergy" with respect to Jelmoli's travel unit Imholz.
"You will see that in the next few weeks, decisive things will take place," he said. He added that he would not consider selling Imholz as long as it was not highly profitable.
